catalog_quote: 3.6 Suprasegmental features. Pahari does not have tone system. It differentiates for vowel length (:) and nasalization (~). ... The basic syllable pattern of Pahari is (C) (C) (G) V (X), where G stands for glide and X for consonant. It shows two suprasegmentals: vowel length and nasalization. Pahari is a toneless languagess [sic] ... h) Stress. This is relatively weak in all Bodish and Himalayish languages as well as in the Pahari. The stress is placed on the word boundary position in Pahari.
world_status: statement found in an open source

Pahari is a toneless languagess'; PDF p. 347 (printed 323), sec. 13.2.1 'h) Stress / This is relatively weak in all Bodish and Himalayish languages as well as in the Pahari. The stress is placed on the word boundary position in Pahari.' All three passages verbatim as quo…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No lexical tone; the only suprasegmental contrasts described are vowel length and nasalization. Word stress is said to be weak and to fall at a 'word boundary position' (edge unspecified -- initial vs final not stated, no examples); the sentence is boilerplate copied from Regmi's 2007 Bhujel grammar and the phonology chapter itself has no stress section, so no placement rule can be coded from this source.
new_statements.exceptions: None. Only other remark: p. 276 'Stress on the question or verb makes emphatics' (sentence-level emphasis).
new_statements.domain_note: Claim is about the word, made in a typological summary without data; no citation-form vs phrase distinction; no stress marks anywhere in the transcriptions.
new_statements.identity_note: All three opened sources describe the Pahari of Kodku hamlet, Badikhel VDC, Lalitpur district ('Badikhel Pahari', endonym Kodpa/Pahi) = Glottolog dialect Lalitpur Pahari Newari [lali1243] under paha1257; Smith 2022 additionally surveys Kavre/Sindhupalchok settlements (Jamune etc. = jamu1234) but has no phonology. Not to be confused with Indo-Aryan 'Pahari' languages.

sources.note: Ch. 3 Phonology has no stress section; sec. 3.6 'Suprasegmental features' (p. 66) says only: no tone system, contrastive vowel length and nasalization; 3.7 (p. 68) 'two suprasegmentals: vowel length and nasalization. Pahari is a toneless language'. The only placement remark is in the typological summary sec. 13.2.1(h) (p. 323): stress 'relatively weak.. The stress is placed on the word boundary position in Pahari' -- a sentence templated on Regmi 2007's Bhujel grammar, with no data. p. 276: 'Stress on the question or verb makes emphatics' (sentence-level).

sources.citation: Regmi, Dan Raj. 2007. The Bhujel Language. PhD dissertation, Tribhuvan University (TU elibrary 20.500.14540/7724) -- opened only to check the wording of the typological checklist that Shrestha 2010 sec. 13.2.1 copies (not a Pahari source).

sources.note: Its item (h) reads 'Stress is relatively weak in all Bodish and Himalayish languages. So is in Bhujel. The stress is placed on the root at the word boundary position in Bhujel (see 3.5.1 for details)' -- showing Shrestha's Pahari sentence is boilerplate with 'on the root' and the cross-reference dropped.
